claims.text: The NiFeCoCrPd alloy family exhibits a second-order magnetic transition with a critical temperature tunable from about 100 K to above room temperature.
Pd addition and heat treatment reduce the distribution of exchange energies and produce a more magnetically homogeneous NiFeCoCr-based alloy.
Nominally FCC Ag or Cu can substitute for Pd and provide similar magnetic tunability because the additive's role is predominantly structural.
Narrowing the distribution of magnetic exchange interactions sharpens the second-order magnetic transition.
A sharper and more homogeneous magnetic transition enhances magnetic entropy change and refrigerant capacity at low applied fields.
The proposed alloys provide a strong magnetocaloric response at approximately 1 T or below.
Intrinsic lattice distortions and high configurational entropy promote rapid heat diffusion.
Intrinsic lattice distortions and multicomponent mixing promote low magnetic hysteresis during cyclic magnetization.
The high-entropy NiFeCoCr-based matrix provides robust mechanical stability or superior mechanical properties.
An as-cast or as-rolled NiFeCoCr alloy containing approximately 3–5 at.% Pd has a relatively broad exchange-energy distribution and substantial structural defects.
FCC-metal substitution followed by heat treatment reduces defect density and decreases X-ray diffraction peak broadening.
XRD peak FWHM is a proxy for the width of the magnetic exchange-energy distribution.
Ag- or Cu-substituted, heat-treated alloys will have a larger low-field magnetic entropy change than the stated baseline.
Ag- or Cu-substituted, heat-treated alloys will have greater refrigerant capacity than the stated baseline.
Ag- or Cu-substituted, heat-treated alloys will have lower M–H hysteresis than the stated baseline.
Ag- or Cu-substituted, heat-treated alloys will maintain or improve mechanical properties relative to the stated baseline.
The mechanism should remain valid in similar transition-metal HEAs at additive concentrations up to approximately 10 at.%, temperatures of about 300–350 K, and fields below 1–2 T.
Magnetic-refrigeration materials require not only a large magnetic entropy change but also adequate heat transfer, thermal conductivity, mechanical and chemical stability, and low hysteresis losses.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as having minimal post-processing heat treatment, whereas the falsification design says both the substituted alloys and controls undergo identical heat treatment protocols.

The initial material contains 3–5 at.% Pd and the intervention replaces that Pd, but the baseline/control is variously described as having no additional FCC substitution, minimal additive, or the baseline composition. It is therefore unclear whether the decisive comparator is Pd-containing NiFeCoCr, additive-free NiFeCoCr, or another minimally alloyed composition.
The control is described as being in the as-cast state, but the same design subsequently states that both sets undergo heat treatment; the control cannot remain strictly as-cast after that treatment.
